3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Sordish law dictated that if a Vice President failed to complete his term, new candidates were to be put forward by the members of the cabinet.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: It was up to me to decide who would fill Petr's shoes. I wanted to chat with them one on one before making my decision.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: After much deliberation, the list had been narrowed down to three. Lucian Galade was the front-runner, followed by Gloria Tory and Albin Clavin.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: I had just begun to settle at my desk when I heard a knock at the door. Lucian entered and perched on the chair across from me.

9.speaker: Player
9.text: “So. Vice President Galade. What do you think?”

10.speaker: Player
10.text: "All right, Lucian. You're one hell of a strategist, but why should I make you VP?"

11.speaker: Lucian Galade
11.text: "You already know what I think, Mr. President."

13.speaker: Lucian Galade
13.text: “In my current capacity as chief strategist, I have evaluated the experience and capabilities of your potential vice presidents. Objectively, I am by far the most qualified candidate."

14.speaker: Lucian Galade
14.text: “I would advise you not only to think about our long history together, but also the many crises I have helped shepherd you through."

15.speaker: Lucian Galade
15.text: “I won't say much beyond that. I believe my work speaks for itself."

16.speaker: Player
16.text: “You're such a valuable strategist. I don't know if I can afford to lose you in that capacity.”

17.speaker: Player
17.text: “I don't know. The public might gossip about your lack of a wife."

18.speaker: Player
18.text: “You wanted Petr's job from day one. How do I know you won't try to have me ousted next?"

19.speaker: Lucian Galade
19.text: “Considering where Petr Vectern's proclivities got us, a vice president who's wholly uninterested in matters of the flesh would be a refreshing change."

20.speaker: Lucian Galade
20.text: “As Vice President, my ability to serve you and this administration will only increase.”

21.speaker: Lucian Galade
21.text: “Mr. Vectern proved himself unfit for the position with his selfish and unprofessional behavior. I am counting on you not to do the same."

22.speaker: Narrator
22.text: Lucian got up from his chair.

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: He left my office. Just a minute later, there was another knock at the door and Gloria Tory came in.

25.speaker: Gloria Tory
25.text: “I must say I was not surprised at all when my name was put forward.”

28.speaker: Player
28.text: “So, Gloria, tell me why I should pick you.”

30.speaker: Gloria Tory
30.text: “One does learn to expect a few things after spending so many years in government.”

31.speaker: Gloria Tory
31.text: “To put it simply, what I bring to the table is years of experience.”

32.speaker: Gloria Tory
32.text: “I have been a member of the Assembly for almost 20 years and I spent 7 years as its Speaker. This alone speaks for itself.”

33.speaker: Gloria Tory
33.text: “And as you know, I am also the spokesperson of the party, as well as the leader of the conservative wing. You can see what I am getting at.”

34.speaker: Player
34.text: “Tell me. What are you getting at?”

35.speaker: Player
35.text: “Your experience would be a great asset.”

36.speaker: Player
36.text: “You become the Vice President, and I get the votes from the conservatives.”

40.speaker: Gloria Tory
40.text: “And so is being able to rally the Assembly's conservative voters to your side."

41.speaker: Gloria Tory
41.text: “I will be blunt. Being the leader of the conservative wing means that if I am the Vice President, we would have more votes.”

42.speaker: Gloria Tory
42.text: “This would allow us to pass bills far more easily. Especially if those bills are aligned to my bloc's causes.”

46.speaker: Gloria Tory
46.text: “Before outright refusing, I insist you at least think about it. Unifying the party instead of fracturing it would certainly be better for the future of the USP."

47.speaker: Gloria Tory
47.text: “Then that makes things easier, doesn't it?"

48.speaker: Gloria Tory
48.text: “I want you to know that I value order over everything else, Mr. President.”

49.speaker: Gloria Tory
49.text: “Being the Speaker of the Assembly requires principles, nerves like steel and determination to uphold proper conduct.”

50.speaker: Gloria Tory
50.text: “You can expect to see the same of my vice presidency."

51.speaker: Gloria Tory
51.text: “Not just any woman. A strong woman who was able to protect order in a roomful of unruly men for 7 years."

52.speaker: Gloria Tory
52.text: “Think about the message it would send. The first woman Vice President of Sordland. No. The first woman Vice President in the whole continent!”

53.speaker: Gloria Tory
53.text: “What support you would lose among traditionalists, you would gain tenfold among Sordish women.”

54.speaker: Player
54.text: “That will be all for now. Thank you.”

55.speaker: Player
55.text: “You are right. There is much to gain. I will consider it.”

56.speaker: Player
56.text: “I'd rather not align myself with the conservative wing.”

57.speaker: Gloria Tory
57.text: “There is much to gain from selecting me, Mr. President. I believe you will make the right choice.”

58.speaker: Gloria Tory
58.text: “A shame, then. I had hoped you would see the opportunity. I guess you lack the experience to do so.”

59.speaker: Gloria Tory
59.text: “I wish you a nice day, Mr. President.”

62.speaker: Narrator
62.text: Gloria made her way out. A minute later, there was another knock at the door. This time, it was Albin Clavin's turn.

66.speaker: Albin Clavin
66.text: "It's a great honor to have been chosen as a candidate. Really terrific."

67.speaker: Player
67.text: “I will be straightforward. Why should I pick you?”

68.speaker: Albin Clavin
68.text: “As you know, I represent the reformist wing of the party.”

69.speaker: Albin Clavin
69.text: “I hope to satisfy the requirements of this sacred position.”

70.speaker: Albin Clavin
70.text: “What Sordland needs today is not only to catch up to our more modern neighbors, but to surpass them.”

71.speaker: Albin Clavin
71.text: “I believe we can do that. No. I am sure!”

72.speaker: Albin Clavin
72.text: “However, this will only be possible if we set aside our differences and unite as one. That is the outlook I wish to bring to the position of Vice President.”

73.speaker: Albin Clavin
73.text: “So that Sordland can excel and soar to new heights.”

75.speaker: Player
75.text: “I did not ask about your opinions. What can you provide me with?”

76.speaker: Player
76.text: “Nonsense. Sordland thrives on tradition. Striving for modernity will get us nowhere."

79.speaker: Albin Clavin
79.text: “The fact is, if I am the Vice President, reformist members of our party will be more likely to support you and your causes."

81.speaker: Albin Clavin
81.text: “This will smooth the passage of bills and help move our administration and our country forward in record time.”

83.speaker: Player
83.text: “*If* you join the administration, that is. I don't think that's likely."

85.speaker: Albin Clavin
85.text: “As unlikely as it is, we all must try.”

86.speaker: Albin Clavin
86.text: “And now what this country needs is more dynamic, youthful leadership.”

87.speaker: Albin Clavin
87.text: “Look at you, President Rayne. You became the youngest member of the Assembly and completely rejuvenated Sordish politics. I want to do the same.”

88.speaker: Albin Clavin
88.text: “Not that you might have forgotten, but I would also like to remind you that you promised me a position in exchange for my support at the Assembly.”

96.speaker: Albin Clavin
96.text: “I always took you for a man of honor.”

97.speaker: Albin Clavin
97.text: “We need to be able to take risks to make gains and that is only possible with a forward-looking perspective."

98.speaker: Albin Clavin
98.text: “A promise once given has to be kept, Mr. President. It would be foolish to go back on your word at this point."

100.speaker: Player
100.text: “Aligning myself with the reformist wing does not seem like the way forward.”

101.speaker: Player
101.text: “Thank you. I will consider what you said."

102.speaker: Player
102.text: “This will be all for now. Thank you.”

103.speaker: Albin Clavin
103.text: “You're quite wrong there -- opposing our views will send Sordland backwards. I thought you would understand."

106.speaker: Narrator
106.text: I leaned back in my chair, thinking about the pros and cons of each of my vice presidential candidates.

108.speaker: Narrator
108.text: I could almost hear Petr's voice in my head, laughing at the absurdity of my situation.

109.speaker: Narrator
109.text: But of course, he wasn't there.

119.speaker: Narrator
119.text: At the entrance to my office, my new secretary Sylvia took my hat and coat. She was a matronly woman in her forties. She had a spotless background assisting various Maroon Palace officials.
119.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_Detained_Petr"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_SecretState_ArrestPetr"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrTrialled"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrSelfResigned"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrForcedResign"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_SecretState_Kill_Petr"] == true) == false)

120.speaker: Narrator
120.text: Replacing Livia had been easy. But replacing my Vice President would be difficult.

124.speaker: Narrator
124.text: After much deliberation, the list had been narrowed down to two. Lucian Galade was the front-runner; Albin Clavin the second choice.

125.speaker: Lucian Galade
125.text: "I expect you will make the right decision."

132.speaker: Lucian Galade
132.text: "Gloria Tory would be the only other suitable possibility, were she not already committed to her position on the Supreme Court."

136.speaker: Lucian Galade
136.text: "It is precisely in my capacity as strategist that I have evaluated the experience and capabilities of your potential vice presidents. Objectively, I am by far the most qualified candidate."

140.speaker: Lucian Galade
140.text: "Even when we have not seen eye to eye, you must admit that my instincts have been unfailingly correct."

141.speaker: Narrator
141.text: He left my office. Just a minute later, there was another knock at the door and Albin Clavin came in.

142.speaker: Player
142.text: "You being a woman could also prove advantageous."

143.speaker: Player
143.text: "I don't think Sordland's ready for a female vice president."

144.speaker: Gloria Tory
144.text: “I'm not just any woman, Mr. Rayne. I was able to protect order in a roomful of unruly men for 7 years."

145.speaker: Gloria Tory
145.text: “And think about the message it would send. The first woman Vice President in the whole continent! What support you would lose among traditionalists, you would gain tenfold among Sordish women."

156.speaker: Albin Clavin
156.text: “I think you already know the answer...”

161.speaker: Gloria Tory
161.text: "This would be your chance to make amends with the party, Mr. Rayne."

165.speaker: Player
165.text: "I simply can't forget that you worked against our constitutional reforms, Ms. Tory. I don't think we are aligned."

166.speaker: Gloria Tory
166.text: "I understand. But that is politics, Mr. President."

171.speaker: Player
171.text: "Do you mean like the constitutional proposal where you didn't even say a word when Ms. Tory confronted me?"

172.speaker: Albin Clavin
172.text: "Come on, Mr. President. You knew my position there. There was nothing I could do to help you."

173.speaker: Albin Clavin
173.text: "But I believe we can achieve great things together."

177.speaker: Albin Clavin
177.text: "Besides, it all worked out great in the end, didn't it? We have successfully changed the constitution. Together."

197.speaker: Albin Clavin
197.text: "Come on, Mr. President. You knew there wasn't anything I could do then."

198.speaker: Albin Clavin
198.text: "My efforts may not have been enough, but that doesn't mean I did not vote for your proposal."

199.speaker: Albin Clavin
199.text: "And I still believe we can work together."

200.speaker: Player
200.text: "I don't think you have a chance, Mr. Clavin."

205.speaker: Player
205.text: "And what have you been doing while the party has been obstructing my every move?"

206.speaker: Albin Clavin
206.text: “Mr. President. I've been fighting my own fight against the establishment within the party.”

207.speaker: Albin Clavin
207.text: "The USP reformists aren't really a part of that."
